records.title: Tire size
records.summary: Read the definition, check the source and bring a better question to your installer.
paragraphs: A metric size combines nominal width, aspect ratio, construction and wheel diameter.
Copy the complete marking and vehicle specification before comparing options.
A decoded size alone does not establish suitability.

records.title: Aspect ratio
records.summary: Read the definition, check the source and bring a better question to your installer.
paragraphs: Aspect ratio is sidewall height expressed as a percentage of nominal width.
Compare the ratio together with the complete size.
The number is not a height in millimeters.

records.title: Wheel diameter and radial construction
records.summary: Read the definition, check the source and bring a better question to your installer.
paragraphs: R identifies radial construction; the following number specifies wheel diameter in inches.
Record both fields when requesting a quote.
Wheel diameter and overall tire diameter are different measurements.

records.title: Load index
records.summary: Read the definition, check the source and bring a better question to your installer.
paragraphs: Load index is a code referring to load capacity under specified conditions.
Ask which verified load specification supports a proposed replacement.
This page does not convert the code into a vehicle-specific load approval.

records.title: Speed rating
records.summary: Read the definition, check the source and bring a better question to your installer.
paragraphs: A speed symbol identifies a standardized speed capability under test conditions.
Ask the installer to document the required specification.
It is not a recommended driving speed.

records.title: XL and load range
records.summary: Read the definition, check the source and bring a better question to your installer.
paragraphs: XL and load range describe load-related tire specifications.
Ask for the complete load and inflation requirements for the proposed tire.
A label alone does not validate a replacement.

references.title: USTMA: tire care and safety guide

records.title: P-metric versus LT
records.summary: Read the definition, check the source and bring a better question to your installer.
paragraphs: P and LT identify different passenger and light-truck tire designations.
Include the designation in the information you give an installer.
These designations are not automatically interchangeable.

records.title: UTQG treadwear
records.summary: Read the definition, check the source and bring a better question to your installer.
paragraphs: UTQG treadwear is a comparative laboratory wear grade, not a mileage guarantee.
Keep the grade separate from a written mileage warranty.
A higher number does not promise a particular service life.

records.title: UTQG traction
records.summary: Read the definition, check the source and bring a better question to your installer.
paragraphs: UTQG traction grades describe straight-line wet braking under controlled test conditions.
Ask what additional evidence supports the driving conditions you care about.
The grade does not summarize every kind of grip.

records.title: Temperature grade
records.summary: Read the definition, check the source and bring a better question to your installer.
paragraphs: UTQG temperature grades concern heat resistance under controlled test conditions.
Read the grade with the rest of the specification.
It is not a weather forecast or an operating-temperature guarantee.

records.title: M+S
records.summary: Read the definition, check the source and bring a better question to your installer.
paragraphs: M+S is a mud-and-snow marking; it does not establish the same tested snow performance as 3PMSF.
Check the actual sidewall symbols when discussing winter use.
The letters alone are not a severe-snow performance certification.

records.title: 3PMSF
records.summary: Read the definition, check the source and bring a better question to your installer.
paragraphs: The three-peak mountain snowflake identifies tires meeting specified snow traction tests.
Ask which marking is present on the exact tire being offered.
The symbol does not certify every winter condition or every vehicle.

records.title: All-season tires
records.summary: Read the definition, check the source and bring a better question to your installer.
paragraphs: All-season tires balance use across varied conditions, with limitations in severe winter weather.
Describe the seasons and routes you actually drive.
The category name alone does not answer a winter suitability question.

records.title: All-weather tires
records.summary: Read the definition, check the source and bring a better question to your installer.
paragraphs: Check the actual snow-performance marking rather than relying only on an all-weather category name.
Ask the seller to show the exact tire specification and symbols.
A product category is not a substitute for documented evidence.

records.title: Winter tires
records.summary: Read the definition, check the source and bring a better question to your installer.
paragraphs: Winter tires are designed for cold-weather and winter-road conditions.
Discuss a seasonal plan with a qualified installer.
A general category description does not approve a particular fitment.

records.title: Summer tires
records.summary: Read the definition, check the source and bring a better question to your installer.
paragraphs: Summer tires target warmer conditions and are not intended for freezing winter use.
Include cold-weather exposure in the conversation before choosing a tire type.
Dry-road performance does not establish winter suitability.

records.title: DOT date
records.summary: Read the definition, check the source and bring a better question to your installer.
paragraphs: The final date digits of the tire identification number identify production week and year.
Record the code when asking about age, storage and manufacturer guidance.
A date code alone does not determine a tire condition assessment.

records.title: Tread depth
records.summary: Read the definition, check the source and bring a better question to your installer.
paragraphs: Tread depth describes the remaining groove depth; wear indicators help identify worn tread.
Ask for measured readings across each tire and an explanation of unusual wear.
A visual impression is not a complete tire inspection.

records.title: Cold pressure and TPMS
records.summary: Read the definition, check the source and bring a better question to your installer.
paragraphs: Use the vehicle tire-information label and manufacturer instructions for cold inflation pressure; TPMS warns of pressure issues.
Ask which vehicle-specific source is being used.
A warning system does not replace regular pressure checks.

records.title: Rotation
records.summary: Read the definition, check the source and bring a better question to your installer.
paragraphs: Rotation changes tire positions according to an appropriate vehicle and tire service schedule.
Ask for the applicable pattern, interval and service record.
One pattern does not apply to every configuration.

records.title: Alignment
records.summary: Read the definition, check the source and bring a better question to your installer.
paragraphs: Alignment concerns wheel geometry; balancing concerns uneven rotating mass.
Ask for measurements and the reason a service is proposed.
These are different services, so request separate explanations.

references.title: USTMA: tire care and safety guide

records.title: AWD and matching tires
records.summary: Read the definition, check the source and bring a better question to your installer.
paragraphs: Matching requirements depend on the vehicle manufacturer and its drivetrain specifications.
Ask which documented rule applies before replacing fewer than a full set.
A generic percentage or rule of thumb is not vehicle-specific approval.

records.title: Run-flat tires
records.summary: Read the definition, check the source and bring a better question to your installer.
paragraphs: Run-flat designs provide limited mobility after pressure loss within manufacturer-defined limits.
Ask about the exact tire, vehicle requirements and post-event inspection.
This term does not authorize continued driving without checking the applicable instructions.

records.title: EV considerations
records.summary: Read the definition, check the source and bring a better question to your installer.
paragraphs: EV tire selection involves load requirements, rolling resistance, noise and vehicle-specific specifications.
Discuss the tradeoffs for your exact vehicle and driving priorities.
An EV marketing label alone does not prove compatibility.

records.title: Installed cost and warranties
records.summary: Read the definition, check the source and bring a better question to your installer.
paragraphs: Compare a written installed total and separately documented warranty terms, exclusions and service obligations.
Ask what is included, conditional, optional or still unknown.
The lowest advertised tire price is not necessarily the lowest installed total.

records.title: Understand the details.
records.summary: Start with tire markings, maintenance terms and questions to take to a qualified professional.
paragraphs: Use the glossary to understand a term. The size decoder explains a supported metric marking; it does not verify fitment.
A saved assessment separates recorded evidence, preferences, prices and gaps. Tire condition still needs an appropriate physical inspection.

references.title: Tires & Tread: reviewed content and publication design

records.title: A practical tire glossary.
records.summary: Twenty-five starting points for understanding tire terminology.
paragraphs: Choose a term to read its definition and source. Definitions describe terminology and do not establish that a specific tire is suitable for a vehicle.

references.title: Tires & Tread: reviewed content and publication design

records.title: Read the marking.
records.summary: Decode a metric tire-size marking without guessing vehicle compatibility.
paragraphs: Enter a marking such as 235/60R18 103H. Unknown formats remain unsupported. Load and speed codes remain codes; the tool does not invent capacity tables.

records.title: Bring the right questions.
records.summary: A checklist for recording what a seller can document.
paragraphs: Keep unknown answers visible. A completed checklist records a conversation; it is not a mechanical inspection, fitment approval or safety certificate.

references.title: Tires & Tread: reviewed content and publication design

questions.question: What is the complete out-the-door price?
questions.goodAnswer: An itemized total identifies required charges, taxes and optional services.
redFlags: Unexplained fees or an incomplete total.

questions.question: What is the tire age and DOT date code?
questions.goodAnswer: The installer records the offered tires’ codes and explains applicable manufacturer age guidance.
redFlags: A date or condition question left unanswered.

questions.question: Do the load and speed ratings meet the vehicle requirements?
questions.goodAnswer: The exact tire specification is checked against the applicable vehicle documentation.

questions.question: Why is this tire being recommended?
questions.goodAnswer: The explanation connects documented features and limitations to your stated needs.
redFlags: A recommendation without reasons or evidence.

questions.question: What are the warranty terms?
questions.goodAnswer: Written terms identify eligibility, exclusions, obligations and the claim process.
redFlags: A mileage promise without its conditions.

questions.question: What rotation and balancing services are included?
questions.goodAnswer: The quote and schedule distinguish included services from later charges.
redFlags: Rotation and balancing treated as the same service.

questions.question: What evidence supports an alignment recommendation?
questions.goodAnswer: The shop explains measurements, symptoms and the proposed work.
redFlags: A service recommendation without an explanation.

questions.question: Where should two new tires go on this vehicle?
questions.goodAnswer: The shop explains the applicable vehicle and tire manufacturer guidance.
redFlags: A universal placement rule offered without checking the configuration.

questions.question: What matching rules apply to this AWD system?
questions.goodAnswer: The shop identifies the vehicle-specific requirements and records the measurements.
redFlags: A generic tolerance offered as vehicle approval.

questions.question: Will the set meet all matching requirements?
questions.goodAnswer: The shop checks the complete specifications and any approved staggered arrangement.
redFlags: Only the marketing model name is compared.

questions.question: Which source sets the inflation pressure?
questions.goodAnswer: The shop identifies the vehicle label or applicable manufacturer instructions.
redFlags: The sidewall maximum used as a universal target.

questions.question: How will lug-nut torque be set and documented?
questions.goodAnswer: The shop identifies and follows the vehicle or wheel manufacturer specification and procedure.
redFlags: A value asserted without an applicable specification.

questions.question: What does road-hazard coverage include?
questions.goodAnswer: Written coverage, exclusions, charges and claim conditions are explained separately.
redFlags: Optional coverage represented as an unconditional guarantee.

questions.question: What is the return or trial policy?
questions.goodAnswer: Written deadlines, condition requirements, fees and exclusions are available before purchase.
redFlags: A verbal assurance without the policy.

records.title: Clear reasons. Visible gaps.
records.summary: How evidence and preferences inform a saved assessment.
paragraphs: Fitment restrictions and known exclusions come before preference scoring. Preference scores describe an ordering, not a promise of safety.
Recorded prices and installed-cost assumptions remain historical. A private quote may include installation or tax in its base amount; it is not automatically a tires-only breakdown.
Advertising and affiliate arrangements do not change recommendation order. Unsupported or missing evidence remains explicit.

references.title: Tires & Tread: reviewed content and publication design

records.title: Know what supports the result.
records.summary: Sources, dates, permissions and limits should be visible.
paragraphs: Reports bind their saved input, evidence and calculation versions. Later changes do not silently rewrite a saved report.
Optional delivery and offers use separate choices. Private reports and capability links are excluded from public education pages and search listings.
Specialist review, licensed coverage and live release acceptance are separate decisions. Local examples do not satisfy those decisions.

references.title: Tires & Tread: reviewed content and publication design

records.title: Find the right next step.
records.summary: Get help with a tire question or a recorded result.
paragraphs: For vehicle-specific tire requirements or a physical tire concern, contact the vehicle manufacturer or a qualified tire professional.
For recall information, consult the official NHTSA tire resource. Keep the tire identification details available.
Use the feedback control on a saved report to describe a result issue. Avoid placing contact details, private report links or other sensitive information in general feedback.
